review_note: At line 7702 the original assumes an open immersion of Noetherian schemes, a Deligne system with constant restriction K and bounded coherent L; its conclusion is colim Hom_X(K_n,L)=Hom_U(K,L|U). The reconstruction retains the colimit direction, coherent derived categories and the restriction.
statement:
For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. Let $(K_n)$ be a Deligne system for $U\subset X$ with common restriction $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$, and let $L\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$. Then restriction induces an isomorphism
\[
\operatorname*{colim}_{n}\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(U)}(K,L|_U).
\]
The colimit maps are defined by precomposition with transitions $K_{n+1}\to K_n$, not by passing to an inverse limit.
hypotheses: Noetherian j:U→X, Deligne system K_n for K, bounded coherent L on X.
conclusions: Filtered colimit of Hom from Deligne system equals Hom from its restriction on U.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lift-map}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes.
Let $(K_n)$ be a Deligne system and denote
$K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_U)$ the value
of the constant system $(K_n|_U)$. Let $L$ be an object of
$D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Then $\colim \Hom_X(K_n, L) = \Hom_U(K, L|_U)$.

The draft preserves all three and distinguishes pro-morphism from levelwise maps.
statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. For the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ of Noetherian schemes: (1) if $(K_n)$ and $(L_n)$ are Deligne systems with constant restriction values $K,L$ on $U$, any morphism $\alpha:K\to L$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ extends to a **unique morphism of pro-objects** $(K_n)\to(L_n)$ that restricts to $\alpha$ (not necessarily a levelwise map with matching indices); (2) every $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ occurs as the common restriction value of some Deligne system on $X$; and (3) such a pro-object is unique up to the unique pro-isomorphism inducing the identity on $K$. Thus $K\mapsto(K_n)$ defines the coherent pro-extension functor $Rj_!$.
hypotheses: Noetherian open immersion, Deligne systems, bounded coherent derived restrictions.
conclusions: Unique pro extension of morphisms, existence of systems, and uniqueness up to pro-isomorphism.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extension-by-zero}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $(K_n)$ and $(L_n)$ be Deligne systems.
Let $K$ and $L$ be the values of the constant systems
$(K_n|_U)$ and $(L_n|_U)$. Given a morphism $\alpha : K \to L$
of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$
there is a unique morphism of pro-systems $(K_n) \to (L_n)$
of $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\alpha$.
\item Given $K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_U)$ there exists a
Deligne system $(K_n)$ such that $(K_n|_U)$ is constant
with value $K$.
\item The pro-object $(K_n)$ of $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
of (2) is unique up to unique isomorphism (as a pro-object).
\end{enumerate}

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extension-by-zero-triangle}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes. Let
$$
K \to L \to M \to K[1]
$$
be a distinguished triangle of $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_U)$.
Then there exists an inverse system of distinguished triangles
$$
K_n \to L_n \to M_n \to K_n[1]
$$
in $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ such that $(K_n)$, $(L_n)$, $(M_n)$
are Deligne systems and such that the restriction of these
distinguished triangles to $U$ is isomorphic to the distinguished triangle
we started out with.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-deligne-system-2-out-of-3}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes.
Let
$$
K_n \to L_n \to M_n \to K_n[1]
$$
be an inverse system of distinguished triangles in
$D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$. If $(K_n)$ and $(M_n)$
are pro-isomorphic to Deligne systems, then so is $(L_n)$.

statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. Fix a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with $V(\mathcal I)=X\setminus U$. Let $(K_n)$ be an inverse system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ with a *uniform* cohomological amplitude $[a,b]$, i.e. $H^i(K_n)=0$ for all $n$ when $i\notin[a,b]$. Then the following are equivalent: (1) $(K_n)$ is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system for $U\subseteq X$; (2) for every $p\in\mathbf Z$ there is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F_p$ such that the inverse systems of coherent sheaves $(H^p(K_n))_n$ and $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_p)_n$ are isomorphic as pro-objects. This condition is independent of the choice of coherent $\mathcal F_p$ and only finitely many $p$ are nonzero due to $[a,b]$.
hypotheses: Noetherian open immersion, fixed ideal I cutting out complement, uniformly bounded inverse system K_n.
conclusions: Deligne-pro-isomorphism characterized by I-adic cohomology pro-systems.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-extension-by-zero-algebra}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes.
Let $a \leq b$ be integers. Let $(K_n)$ be an inverse system of
$D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
such that $H^i(K_n) = 0$ for $i \not \in [a, b]$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(K_n)$ is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system,
\item for every $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ there exists a coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ such that the pro-systems
$(H^p(K_n))$ and $(\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{F})$ are pro-isomorphic.
\end{enumerate}

statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. Let $X=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_r$ be a **finite** open cover and $(K_n)$ an inverse system of $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$. Then $(K_n)$ is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system for $U\subset X$ iff for each $i$ its restricted system $(K_n|_{W_i})$ is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system for the induced open immersion $U\cap W_i\hookrightarrow W_i$. This is *finite-cover locality* of Deligne-system pro-isomorphism, not a claim about arbitrary unindexed covers.
hypotheses: Noetherian j:U→X, finite open cover of X and inverse system of bounded-coherent complexes.
conclusions: Deligne-system property is equivalent to its restrictions on each member of finite cover.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-extension-by-zero}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes. Let
$(K_n)$ be an inverse system in $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $X = W_1 \cup \ldots \cup W_r$ be an open covering.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(K_n)$ is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system,
\item for each $i$ the restriction $(K_n|_{W_i})$
is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system with respect to
the open immersion $U \cap W_i \to W_i$.
\end{enumerate}
